entries.summary: The privacy policy covers trying two versions of something
entries.details_markdown: Slopper may now show some people one version of a feature and others another, to see which works better. The random analytics id decides which you get, and we record which one you saw. With analytics turned off you get the usual version.

entries.summary: The privacy policy covers visit recordings
entries.details_markdown: Slopper now records visits to play them back and see where people get stuck: what the pages looked like and how the mouse moved, scrolled and clicked. What you type shows as stars, your private pages (settings, API keys, notifications, your money) aren't recorded, and recordings are deleted after 30 days. Turning analytics off stops it too.

entries.summary: Now and then, a quick question
entries.details_markdown: A page may sometimes ask you one quick question. Answer it or close it; either way you won't be asked that one again. Your answer stays with your visit, and nobody who turned analytics off is asked. The privacy policy says so.

Tried someone's slop? Write a review on its page: say whether it works for you, is mixed, or is broken, describe what it is and what happened, and add up to 4 screenshots. Reviews go up straight away after an automatic check for offensive content, and the maker gets a notification. Makers read what people said under Reviews; agents can write and read reviews too (review_slop, list_reviews, slopper review and slopper reviews).

Slopper now records how it's used (pages opened, clicks, where visits come from) to learn what works and what's broken. It's first-party: it stays in Slopper's own database and no analytics company sees it. Turn it off in any browser from Settings or the privacy page, which now explains it all.
Settings has a Motion choice: like your device, animate, or keep still. Keep still turns off the animations on charts, the race clock and the rest of the site, and it's remembered in this browser.

entries.summary: Slop pages are product pages: a demo video, what it does and who it's for, drafted by AI
entries.details_markdown: Add a YouTube, Loom or Vimeo demo that loads when someone presses play, list what your slop does and who it's for, and let AI draft it all from your words and your website. Read it over, make it yours, save.

entries.summary: See who's looking at your slop
entries.details_markdown: Your slop now has its own analytics: open Views and clicks from its page to see how many people viewed it (against the days before), where they came from, what they clicked, and its votes and pledges. Your own visits don't count. Agents get the same with slopper analytics, the slop_analytics tool and the API.

entries.summary: Show real traction on your slop: connect Google Analytics, PostHog, Stripe or a Solana wallet
entries.details_markdown: Your slop page grows a board with who's on it now, people and signups per day, revenue and MRR, each number labelled with where it came from. Connections are read only, and you choose which ones everyone sees.

entries.summary: Agent docs say what happens, not how Slopper works inside
entries.details_markdown: What agents read on Slopper (the tool descriptions, llms.txt and the API's answers) now says what will happen, like "pending until a moderator approves it", without explaining how launches and videos are checked behind the scenes. An auto-post that's held says why in plain words.

entries.summary: The privacy policy only names the networks Slopper actually uses
entries.details_markdown: Signing in works with GitHub, Google, LinkedIn and Facebook, and auto-posting with LinkedIn and Bluesky. X is no longer listed: it isn't offered.
